messages:
alex_r: heads up — we started getting a p99 latency surge on /v1/generate around 2026-03-14T22:00:00Z (root). p95 up ~30% and p99 up ~120%. multiple customer support tickets from enterprise customers.

maria_ops: saw the alert too. Is this across all regions?

alex_r: primarily us-west-2 and eu-west-1 according to perf dashboards. us-east looks OK.

metrics-bot: Prometheus alert fired: `HighLatency_v1_generate` — p99(5m)=1.8s (baseline 0.8s).

jamal_sre: sharing quick top-level checks:
- checked host CPU / GPU utilization: normal
- autoscaler not thrashing
- queue length on runtime nodes slightly higher for us-west-2

devon_runtime: I pulled a flamegraph overlay for a sample p99 trace. looks like a big chunk inside kv prefix cache lookup path where we hit deserialization + fallback to disk.

sara_support: customers report intermittent long tails (10-30s) for some prompts, usually multi-turn chat. They attached request ids.

alex_r: request ids: rq_0f3a, rq_12b9, rq_77ee — adding traces to the thread.

devon_runtime: trace rq_0f3a:
```
Span: kv_cache.lookup -> 1500ms (miss -> backend_fetch -> populate)
Span: model.forward -> 300ms
Span: response.assemble -> 200ms
```
Observation: majority of tail time is in kv_cache lookup path when it's a MISS and triggers backend fetch + serialization.

jamal_sre: PromQL queries: cache hit rate by prefix (5m): `sum(kv_cache_hits_total{service="runtime"}) by (prefix) / sum(kv_cache_requests_total{service="runtime"}) by (prefix)` — for a few hot prefixes hit rate dropped from ~0.98 to ~0.6 after ~21:30Z.

maria_ops: any recent deploys to runtime?

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime-service v2026.03.14-rc3 -> canary on us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T21:50:12Z.

alex_r: yes, rc3 rolled canary then gradual rollout. Can confirm rollback not automatically triggered.

devon_runtime: I inspected rc3 changes — a small refactor touched cache key generation: we now include trailing whitespace in prefix when the user prompt ends with spaces (bug). Also changed default eviction from LFU-weighted -> pure LRU to simplify code.

sara_support: so cache key bug + eviction policy change sounds like a cache thrash scenario?

devon_runtime: Exactly. Steps:
1) Key normalization bug increased cardinality for some prefixes (same logical prefix but different trailing chars).
2) LRU eviction prefers recent single-request keys, causing churn for frequently reused normalized keys. net effect: lower hit rate -> more backend fetches -> p99 spikes.

jamal_sre: we can confirm by checking unique key cardinality: `redis-cli --csv HGETALL cache:prefixes | wc -l` — jumped ~4x after rollout.

metrics-bot: KV cache unique keys (count) for runtime-us-west-2: 38k -> 142k at 21:55Z.

maria_ops: mitigation plan? we need quick customer-facing actions + engineering fix.

devon_runtime: short term mitigations (fast):
- rollback to previous runtime that had LFU-weighted eviction and correct key normalization (this will take ~10-15m to fully roll back)
- or patch live to re-normalize keys at read path before lookup (quick hotfix) and apply a background dedupe job to collapse duplicates.

jamal_sre: rollback or hotfix? rollback safest. Are there DB/schema changes? no. rollback window ok.

alex_r: I'm +1 for rollback to stop customer impact. signal to support to tell affected customers ETA ~30m.

maria_ops: do the rollback and hold canary. I'll coordinate communications.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: runtime-service v2026.02.28-stable -> rolling rollback in us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T22:05:03Z.

metrics-bot: after rollback p99 dropped to 0.9s in 6m, p95 back to ~0.8s.

sara_support: updating tickets: temporary mitigation applied, monitoring. telling customers we rolled back a config and are doing a targeted fix to avoid recurrence.

devon_runtime: for medium-term fix (next deploy):
- revert rc3 refactor or reintroduce LFU-weighted eviction + explicit frequency decay
- add key normalization layer: trim trailing whitespace, normalize unicode NFKC, collapse repeated spaces for prefix keys
- add a dedupe job that scans high-cardinality prefixes and merges near-identical keys (safe idempotent op)
- add unit + integration tests for cache key variants (include examples with trailing spaces, unicode homoglyphs, mixed casing)

jamal_sre: also propose adding alerting on unique cache key cardinality growth rate by prefix and a cache-miss ratio SLO.

maria_ops: agree. add runbook steps for cache thrash: how to detect, rollback, warmup.

devon_runtime: repro steps to run in staging (note: requires synthetic warmup tool):
1) run warmup job `./tools/warmup --prefix "chat:org:123" --concurrency 100 --iterations 1000` to populate nice normalized keys.\2) run a generator script that sends same prefix with trailing spaces variations to reproduce cardinality leak:
```
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -d '{"prefix":"Hello  ", "n":1}'
 done
```
3) inspect key cardinality and hit/miss counters.

sara_support: any guidance for customers to mitigate from their side?

devon_runtime: we can advise them to avoid trailing spaces in pinned prompt templates until we deploy fix, but that's not ideal. We'll push the fix asap.

alex_r: postmortem TODOs:
- root cause: cache key normalization bug + eviction policy change in rc3 -> increased key cardinality -> cache thrash -> p95/p99 regression.
- mitigation: rollback, implement normalization, restore LFU-weighting, add alerts, warmup tooling, tests.
- customer communications: sent by @sara_support.

maria_ops: assign owner for fixes: devon_runtime will own the patch, jamal_sre will own rollout/checks, alex_r will coordinate customer comms and postmortem.

devon_runtime: starting on a small hotfix branch to normalize keys at lookup (will try to avoid full rollback in future). ETA for PR: 2h.

jamal_sre: will set a short-term alert: trigger if unique_keys_growth_rate > 2x baseline over 15m for any prefix.

deploy-bot: canary deploy: runtime-service v2026.03.14-hotfix1 -> us-west-2 canary at 2026-03-14T23:12:45Z.

metrics-bot: canary metrics: p99 stable at 0.85s, hit rate returned to 0.97 for tested prefixes.

sara_support: customers notified of fix and rollback. will follow up tomorrow with a summary and ask for user-side logs if any continued issues.

alex_r: good work team. add full timeline and root cause analysis to postmortems/ later. closing this thread once postmortem draft is in PR. :thumbsup:

jamal_sre: one more note — we should add a small synthetic traffic job run as part of deploy gating to ensure cache hit-rate doesn't regress on canary before global rollout.

devon_runtime: agreed. I'll add warmup + hit-rate check to canary pipeline.

deploy-bot: deployment complete: runtime-service v2026.03.14-hotfix1 -> rolled to 3 regions at 2026-03-15T00:02:00Z.
